newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends 11 cts higher on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends 11 cts higher on short-covering.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures ended 11 cents higher on Friday on modest short-covering in thin volume, brokers said.
Front month August last traded at $18.07, down from a high of $18.15 touched in mid-afternoon at the peak of a brief rally inspired by stronger NYMEX gasoline.
Some brokers had predicted a volatile close due to unwinding of big options plays but this failed to materialise.
"The market has been short all week awaiting news on whether the Iraqis really are going to sell a they'll sell -- in which case people throught the market would collapse," one broker said.
"But in the end there was no real concrete news to move the market. All week it hasn't moved moved more than 30 cents either side of the range it's been in today."
The gasoline surge was built on gains in the cash gasoline market in Houston derived from a Colonial Pipeline scheduling deadline and possibly also paper market positions.
IPE gas oil futures closed 25 cents higher at $162 a tonne after moving in a range between the low of $161.25 and high of $162.25. Trade was quiet and little affected by gasoline.
Front month August gasoline was at 59.40 cents a gallon, up 0.80 cent on the day but down from the high of 59.90.
The gasoline strength boosted NYMEX crude, which was at $19.34 a barrel after touching a high of $19.44.
Volume in London remained very thin as dealers awaited a meeting on Sunday between the U.N. Iraq coordinator and Iraqi officials for more talks on Baghdad's aid distribution plan.
Prices fell sharply on Thursday when the German government said it planned to sell oil from its reserves in order to qualify for Europe's single currency.
